Bootstrap Inference for the Selected Arm

A. Author
Abstract

We study inference on the mean of the empirically best arm. The standard bootstrap is inconsistent at ties. We propose a smoothed maximum whose temperature vanishes at rate nn^{-1/4} and show uniform coverage.

1 Introduction

Selecting the best of K arms and then reporting its sample mean leads to the winner’s curse. Prior corrections are conservative when arms are nearly tied.

2 Setup

Observations are i.i.d. within each arm with finite fourth moments.

3 Main Results

3.1 Coverage

Theorem 2. The proposed interval achieves uniform asymptotic coverage over the parameter space, including configurations with exact ties.

MethodCoverage

In simulations with 5 arms, coverage is 94.8% against 87.1% for the naive bootstrap.
